issues.title: Test method missing test prefix
issues.description: The rule requires test methods to start with 'test' prefix, but the method 'verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders' does not follow this naming convention
issues.rule_name: Test Classes Must Use XCTest Framework with Proper Structure

issues.title: Incorrect logical operator in tearDown causing theme reset to be skipped for all iPad tests
issues.description: The tearDown method uses OR (||) instead of AND (&&) when checking if the test should skip theme reset. This causes the theme reset to be skipped for ALL tests running on iPad devices, not just the testSelectBottomPlacement test. The original intent was to skip theme reset only when BOTH conditions are true (the test is testSelectBottomPlacement AND it's running on iPad), but the current code skips it when EITHER condition is true. This will leave the theme in Dark mode after any test runs on iPad, potentially affecting subsequent tests that expect Light theme.

issues.title: Insufficient timeout for paste permission dialog causing test flakiness
issues.description: The timeout for the 'Allow Paste' permission dialog button was reduced from 1.5 seconds to 0.5 seconds. This is too short for the iOS permission dialog to appear and be interactable, especially on slower devices or under load. The tapIfExists method waits for the element to exist within the specified timeout before attempting to tap it. A 0.5 second timeout may cause the test to miss the permission dialog entirely, preventing the paste action from completing and causing subsequent assertions to fail when the URL is not populated in the address bar.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
urlBar.pressWithRetry(duration: 2.0, element: pasteAction)
        mozWaitForElementToExist(app.tables["Context Menu"])
        pasteAction.waitAndTap()
        springboard.buttons["Allow Paste"].tapIfExists(timeout: 0.5)
        mozWaitForElementToExist(urlBar)
        mozWaitForValueContains(urlBar, value: url)

issues.title: Long-press duration too short to trigger context menu in bookmark sharing test
issues.description: The pressWithRetry duration was reduced from 1.5 seconds to 0.5 seconds for the long-press gesture on the bookmark item. According to the pressWithRetry implementation, the method performs a long press and expects the specified element (contextMenu) to appear. A 0.5 second press duration is typically insufficient for iOS to recognize a long-press gesture and display the context menu - iOS generally requires at least 1.0-1.5 seconds for long-press recognition. This will cause the context menu to fail to appear, making the subsequent call to tap the share button fail since the contextMenu element won't exist.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
waitForTabsButton()
        navigator.goto(LibraryPanel_Bookmarks)
        // Long-press on a bookmarked website
        let contextMenu = app.tables["Context Menu"]
        app.tables.cells.staticTexts["Example Domain"].pressWithRetry(duration: 0.5, element: contextMenu)
        // Tap the Share button in the context menu
        contextMenu.buttons["shareLarge"].waitAndTap()

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31184 - [MTE-5047] - auto tests improvements

structured_output.summary:
This PR is test-only cleanup in the iOS XCUITest suite. It deletes `OnboardingTests.testWhatsNewPage` (which was already a no-op `XCTSkip`) and removes it from three xctestplans, makes `testSelectBottomPlacement` skip before it taps through Terms of Service on iPad, adds a best-effort "Allow Paste" dismissal to `BaseTestCase.openNewTabAndValidateURLisPaste`, and switches the bookmarks long-press helper in `ShareLongPressTests` to a `pressWithRetry` that waits on the context menu.

The deletion and the paste-helper change are reasonable. The `ShareLongPressTests` press change is a real improvement. Three things block merge. First, the new `OnboardingTests.tearDown` returns early on iPad and for `testSelectBottomPlacement`, which skips `app.terminate()` and `super.tearDown()` for those tests. Second, the same early return drops the Light-theme reset for every test on iPad, which leaks Dark mode into later tests (`testFirstRunTourDarkMode` sets Dark and relies on teardown). Third, renaming `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` to `verify...` means XCTest never runs it, and the Accessibility test plan still names the old method, so this coverage is silently gone rather than fixed.

I did not run the suite; the iPad and flakiness claims are inferred from the code, not observed on a device.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The teardown early return skips required XCTest cleanup for every iPad run and every `testSelectBottomPlacement` run, and it also disables the theme reset on iPad. The method rename silently disables a test that the Accessibility plan still references. Each is a small, local fix, but they change what runs and what state leaks, so they should be addressed before merge.

architecture.overview:
The XCUITest suite is built on `BaseTestCase`, which provides `tearDown` (terminate the app, then call `super.tearDown()`), XCUIElement helpers such as `pressWithRetry` and `tapIfExists`, and `switchThemeToDarkOrLight`. Test classes such as `OnboardingTests` and `ShareLongPressTests` subclass it. Test plans (`AccessibilityTestPlan.xctestplan`, `Smoketest.xctestplan`, `TAESmokeTestPlan.xctestplan`) select tests by identifier, for example `ShareLongPressTests/testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders()`.

The PR changes three things. It deletes a test that was already skipped and drops its plan entries. It moves the iPad skip in `testSelectBottomPlacement` ahead of the Terms of Service tap, and it adds a teardown early exit for iPad and that test. It also changes two test helpers: a paste-dialog dismissal in `BaseTestCase` and a context-menu-aware long press in `ShareLongPressTests`. The teardown change touches every test in `OnboardingTests`, so it has the widest effect.
steps: Entry point: XCTest runs each `test*` method on a `BaseTestCase` subclass. Each subclass's `tearDown` must end by calling `app.terminate()` and `super.tearDown()` so the next test starts clean.

`OnboardingTests.tearDown` (lines 27-38) now returns early when the test name contains `testSelectBottomPlacement` or the device is an iPad. That early return skips both the theme reset and the base teardown.

`testFirstRunTourDarkMode` (lines 148-155) switches the theme to Dark and relies on `tearDown` to restore Light. This test has no iPad guard, so on iPad it now leaves the app in Dark mode for later tests.

`ShareLongPressTests` renames the bookmarks Reminders test to a `verify...` method (line 47). XCTest only discovers `test`-prefixed methods, and the Accessibility plan still lists the old name, so the flow is no longer exercised.

The bookmarks long-press helper (lines 246-249) now waits on the `Context Menu` table through `pressWithRetry` instead of a fixed 1-second press. This is the one change that directly targets flakiness and is sound.
`BaseTestCase.openNewTabAndValidateURLisPaste` (line 471) adds a 0.5 s best-effort tap of an "Allow Paste" SpringBoard button. Its timing and necessity are unverified.

findings.title: tearDown early return skips app.terminate and super.tearDown
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/OnboardingTests.swift`, the `tearDown` override (lines 27-38) returns early when the test name contains `testSelectBottomPlacement` or on iPad. That skips `app.terminate()` and `super.tearDown()`. Change it so only the `switchThemeToDarkOrLight(theme: "Light")` call is conditional, and `app.terminate()` plus `try await super.tearDown()` always run. Keep the `#available(iOS 17.0, *)` guard around the theme reset only. Match the base class pattern in `BaseTestCase.tearDown` (around line 119).

findings.title: iPad now skips the Light-theme reset for all OnboardingTests
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/OnboardingTests.swift`, the `tearDown` override (lines 27-38) skips `switchThemeToDarkOrLight(theme: "Light")` whenever `iPad()` is true. `testFirstRunTourDarkMode` (around lines 148-155) switches to Dark and is not iPad-gated, so Dark mode leaks into later iPad tests. Remove the `iPad()` condition from the theme reset. If a reset is truly unnecessary on iPad, gate it on the test that actually changes the toolbar, not on the device. Keep `app.terminate()` and `super.tearDown()` unconditional.

findings.title: Renamed bookmarks test is never run, and the plan still references the old name
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/ShareLongPressTests.swift`, line 47 renames `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` to `verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders`. XCTest does not discover that name, and `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/AccessibilityTestPlan.xctestplan` line 371 still references the old name. Restore the `test` prefix on the method. If the test needs to be disabled because of flakiness, add an explicit `throw XCTSkip("<reason>")` at the top of the method instead of renaming it. Keep the flakiness fix in `longPressBookmarkAndReachShareOptions` as it is.

findings.title: Name-based check in tearDown is unnecessary and its comment is misleading
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/OnboardingTests.swift`, the `tearDown` at line 29 checks `self.name.contains("testSelectBottomPlacement")` before skipping the theme reset. `testSelectBottomPlacement` never changes the theme, so that clause is dead logic. Remove it, and keep the theme-reset condition only if it is still required after the separate teardown fix. Make sure the comment on line 30 matches the code it sits above.

findings.title: Use throw XCTSkip instead of XCTSkipIf with an always-true flag
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/OnboardingTests.swift`, `testSelectBottomPlacement` (around lines 348-352) uses `let shouldSkipTest = true` and `try XCTSkipIf(shouldSkipTest, ...)` inside an `if iPad()` block. Replace that with `throw XCTSkip("Toolbar option not available for iPad")` directly inside the `if iPad()` block. Keep the check before the Terms of Service tap, as it is now.

findings.title: Fixed 0.5 s wait for the Allow Paste prompt may not be enough
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/BaseTestCase.swift`, `openNewTabAndValidateURLisPaste` (line 471) calls `springboard.buttons["Allow Paste"].tapIfExists(timeout: 0.5)`. A 0.5 s window may miss the prompt, and the wait adds delay on every run. Confirm from a device run whether the prompt appears on the SpringBoard process and how long it takes. Then pick a timeout that reflects that (or a named constant), and add a short comment explaining why the prompt is dismissed here.

findings.title: Context-menu-aware long press replaces a fixed press
Deleted test was already skipped and its plan entries were removed consistently
findings.body:
`testWhatsNewPage` started with `throw XCTSkip(...)` and its body was commented out, so deleting it removes no executed coverage. The removal was applied to all three xctestplans, and a repository search finds no remaining references to `testWhatsNewPage`.

One leftover remains: `OpenWhatsNewPage` in `FxScreenGraph.swift` (around line 277) now appears to have no callers. That is a small cleanup for a follow-up, not a blocker.
